toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The slowdown is mostly not Corvane and not the new hires. It comes from one change in the May credit policy: property-secured loans between $150k and $500k now need a full inspection appraisal instead of a desktop valuation. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days and desktop ones about 1.2. The valuation stage for property-secured loans rose from about 1.7 days to 7.6–8.4 days. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days. The valuer's turnaround per appraisal type hasn't changed. Document collection at the new hires' branches matches the other branches, and the Credit Hub's own stages are flat. The policy change was never assessed for its effect on processing time. It was made for a reason: audit found desktop valuations overstated values by a median 12%.

Don't withhold Corvane's payment or put the new hires on improvement plans. Both would punish the wrong party. Take the measured delay and the audit rationale to the credit risk committee and ask it to decide whether to keep, narrow or speed up the full-appraisal rule. Also add a by-stage view to the dashboard.

On withdrawals: part of the rise is likely the new auto-close rule. A third of the closures since May (32 of 73) are auto-closes. Whether the delays cause the other withdrawals is unproven, so hold off on a rebate offer. I'm fairly sure of the main finding.
